content: The test image shows soybean pods split open with seeds that have dark black markings near the hilum, and white/cottony material visible inside the pods. Let me compare with reference images.
The Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus reference shows a very similar split pod with seeds having dark markings near the hilum. Let me check a few more candidates.

**Analysis Summary:**

**Test image observations:**
- Split/open mature soybean pods (brown, hairy/pubescent exterior)
- Seeds are cream/pale-colored and mature
- Seeds have distinct dark **black markings concentrated around/near the hilum**
- Pod interior shows white papery tissue (normal)
- Background shows multiple mature brown pods

**Reference image comparison:**
- **Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus**: Top-right panel shows an almost identical image — open pod with 2 mature seeds having dark/black hilum-centered mottling. **Exact match.**
- **Purple_Seed_Stain**: Seeds show pink/purple discoloration — test image markings are black, not purple.
- **Downy_mildew**: Reference shows leaf symptoms; pod interior described as crusty white fungal mass — not matching.
- **Tobacco_Streak_Virus**: Shows green/immature seeds with discoloration — test image seeds are mature and cream-colored.
- **White_Mold**: Shows white mycelium on external pods/stems — not matching.
- **Phomopsis**: Shriveled/cracked seeds with chalky mold — not matching.
- All leaf-disease classes (Septoria, Frogeye, Soybean rust, etc.) are irrelevant — test image focuses on seeds.

**Conclusion:** The dark black markings radiating from/near the hilum on cream-colored mature seeds inside an open pod is the classic sign of Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus — pigment diffusion from the hilum causing seed coat mottling.
